title: Make the VCF Operations custom-group sync safe to run twice
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Our environment-sync job creates a VCF Operations custom group per managed environment and never checks whether the group is already there. It timed out last night, the on-call re-ran it, and Operations now holds two identical custom groups for every environment we manage. Rebuild the job so that running it again is a no-op.

Build a Python package `opsgroups/` at the workspace root. Use the Python standard library only. No third-party module may be imported anywhere under `opsgroups/`; `urllib.request` and `json` are enough, and `requests`, `httpx`, `urllib3` and the like are out.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not from a documentation page, and not from the 9.1 revision of that same file. The only operationIds in scope are `acquireToken`, `getCustomGroups`, `createCustomGroup` and `modifyCustomGroup`. Read that contract: it carries the request and response schemas, the `Token-based-authorization` security scheme, and the `/suite-api` base path from the specification's server entry. The appliance wants the acquired token as `Authorization: vRealizeOpsToken <token>`, which the contract records under `clientConventions` because the specification declares that header but not its value.

The acceptance harness imports your package and calls:

`opsgroups.ensure_custom_group(base_url, username, password, *, name, adapter_kind_key, resource_kind_key, rules=None, included_resources=None, excluded_resources=None, auto_resolve_membership=None, auth_source=None, timeout=30.0)`

`base_url` already ends in `/suite-api`.

Requirements:

- Sign in. Exchange the credentials for a token with `acquireToken`, exactly once per call, and carry it on every later request. `acquireToken` is the call that mints the token, so it sends no `Authorization` header of its own. `username-password.authSource` is optional: when the caller supplied no `auth_source` it must be absent from the body, never sent as null or as an empty string. Every operation in scope offers `application/json` and `application/xml`, so ask for JSON explicitly rather than taking whatever the appliance prefers, and send JSON bodies as `application/json`.

- Look before you write. Read the existing groups with `getCustomGroups`. Both of its query parameters are optional and neither is wanted here, so the request carries no query string at all. A group is the one being reconciled when its `resourceKey.name`, `resourceKey.adapterKindKey` and `resourceKey.resourceKindKey` all match the desired ones; the same name under another resource kind is a different group and must not be written to.

- Reconcile. No match: create the group with `createCustomGroup`. One match that already says what was asked for: make no write at all. One match that has drifted: send `modifyCustomGroup` carrying that group's existing `custom-group.id`. More than one match, which is exactly what an unguarded repeat leaves behind: raise `OpsConflictError` exposing the colliding identifiers as `.group_ids` and write nothing. The 9.0.0.0 document gives `createCustomGroup` no idempotency key, no conditional-request header and no 409 for a duplicate name, so a bare repeat files a second group; the lookup is what makes the call safe to retry.

- Request body. Send a `custom-group` and nothing beyond it. `resourceKey` carries only `name`, `adapterKindKey` and `resourceKindKey`, so `resourceIdentifiers`, `links` and `extension` stay off the wire. The appliance assigns `id`, so a create carries none and only a modify sends one; `policy` and `links` are never sent. `autoResolveMembership` goes out only when the caller passed a bool, and `False` is a value that was asked for rather than an unset property. `membershipDefinition` is required by the specification, so it is always present, but it holds only what the caller supplied: `rules` from `rules`, `includedResources` from `included_resources`, `excludedResources` from `excluded_resources`, each omitted when nothing or an empty collection was passed, which leaves the member as exactly `{}` when nothing was supplied at all. The specification's own request example sends `includedResources`, `excludedResources` and `custom-group-properties` as empty arrays; do not follow it. An unset optional member is omitted from the JSON, never sent as `null`, `""` or `[]`. `includedResources` and `excludedResources` are declared `uniqueItems`, so deduplicate and sort them and keep the body byte-stable across runs. `rules` travels through unchanged.

- Deciding whether it drifted. The appliance normalises what it stores: a group read back always carries all four `custom-group-membership` members, empty collections included, and its `resource-key` comes back with `resourceIdentifiers` and `links` that nobody sent. None of that is drift. Compare only `autoResolveMembership` and `membershipDefinition`, with null and empty members dropped from both sides, and treat the same resource identifiers in a different order as unchanged. When the caller passed no `auto_resolve_membership`, whatever the appliance already holds is what was asked for.

- Result. Return a dict whose keys are in exactly this order: `action`, one of `created`, `updated` or `unchanged`; `groupId`; `group`, the `custom-group` as the appliance last reported it; and `writes`, the number of `createCustomGroup` plus `modifyCustomGroup` calls the run actually put on the wire.

- Errors. Export `OpsError`, plus `OpsAuthError`, `OpsApiError` and `OpsConflictError` derived from it. A 401 from `acquireToken` raises `OpsAuthError` before any group is read. Any other non-success status raises `OpsApiError` exposing the HTTP status as `.status`. Neither the password nor the acquired token may appear in an exception message.

Acceptance: `python3 verify.py`. It drives your package against a contract-pinned loopback VCF Operations appliance on `127.0.0.1` with dummy credentials, repeats each reconciliation, and reads that fixture's request log to check the exact method, target, query string, headers and JSON body member set of every call, including that each unset optional member was omitted rather than sent empty, and that a repeated run writes nothing and leaves exactly one group behind. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.py`, `mock_ops.py`, `.gitignore` and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
